title: Start the Sentence at a Word
text: In the correct pattern, \w+ starts the match at one or more word characters. This lets the match begin at the first word of each sentence, such as I, So, what, or My.

title: Use a Negated Punctuation Class
text: The piece [**.!?]* means zero or more characters that are not periods, exclamation points, or question marks. This gathers the rest of the sentence without crossing earlier sentence-ending punctuation.

title: Meaning of the Final Quantifier
text: In [.!?]{2,}, how many punctuation marks are required at the end?

title: Why the Anchored Pattern Fails
text: The pattern r"**\w+[.!?]{2,}" starts with **, so it can only match at the beginning of the entire string. It cannot start again in the middle of the string to find later sentences.

title: Putting the Pieces Together
text: The correct pattern uses one or more word characters, then zero or more non-punctuation characters, then two or more sentence-ending punctuation marks: r"\w+[**.!?]*[.!?]{2,}".
